title: Subcontractor selection and safety bridging
description: Complete original VNDRLY L04 guided training with six taught lessons, two worked cases and 26 individually answered questions.
purpose: Prevent lower-tier gaps between service scope and client controls.
practicalBoundary: Identify conflicting rules and responsibility boundaries; bridging case exercise. Written learning does not confer practical competence, a provider credential, employer authorization or Partner/site readiness.

lessons.title: Start here — Subcontractor selection and safety bridging
lessons.body:
# L04: Subcontractor selection and safety bridging

Prevent lower-tier gaps between service scope and client controls. This course teaches the decisions needed to implement that purpose in field operations. It covers scope-specific screening, responsibilities, flowdown, interfaces and monitoring. The examples involve fictional oilfield crews and companies; none is a real incident record or evidence of a company's implementation.

Read six substantive lessons, answer each attached knowledge check, then study two applied cases and answer the twenty final questions. Every question has three choices and one correct answer. The course records the first answer separately from any correction. Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation, including reading the specific explanation for each correction. A remediated result must never replace the original score. There is no speed requirement: take the time needed to explain the decision in your own words.

The audience includes workers who recognize gaps, supervisors who coordinate work and program owners who maintain the system. Each has a different decision boundary. An observer may report an uncertain safeguard without personally being qualified to repair it. A supervisor may coordinate a hold without being the person authorized to clear a technical prerequisite. Learn both the action and the limit on that action.

Company evidence review, practical competence and job/site authorization are separate judgments. A favorable company maturity score does not release an unsafe assignment. These lessons supply original instruction and fictional worked examples; actual technical methods, operating limits, legal applicability and authorizations must come from the competent employer/site sources. Unknown required conditions remain unverified. Do not invent a value, signature, expiry date or successful observation to fill a blank.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Screen the actual subcontract scope
lessons.body:
## Screen the actual subcontract scope

Lower-tier selection starts with the work proposed, not a vendor's overall grade. Identify legal entity, services, locations, workers, equipment and specialist exposures. Compare evidence with those boundaries. A company assessed for routine maintenance may lack confined-space cleaning capability. Commercial approval and safety acceptance answer different questions. Require a specialist review when the scope exceeds the general reviewer's expertise.

### Deeper application

Use a scope statement that another reviewer could test. Pump maintenance at named production locations is more useful than oilfield services, but still needs boundaries around electrical work, entry, lifting and transport if those tasks are proposed. Ask the performing company to identify further tiers and specialty support. When evidence is missing, distinguish unverified capability from a proven unsafe practice. Both can prevent acceptance of the new scope, but the record should state the actual basis rather than exaggerate the finding.

### Worked oilfield example

A maintenance subcontractor adds vessel cleaning to its accepted work without presenting rescue or entry-role evidence. The decision is to hold the added scope and obtain specialist evidence and interface review before mobilization.

Approval for one service does not establish competence or arrangements for a different exposure. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A scope-specific assessment listing vessel-cleaning prerequisites and unresolved rescue interfaces. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the submitted assessment covers another legal entity in the same corporate group. The appropriate correction is to verify the actual performing entity and its matching capability before acceptance. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 — Verify people equipment and evidence
lessons.body:
## Verify people equipment and evidence

Evidence must identify who will do the work, with which equipment and under which limits. Check credential issuer, identity, validity and task coverage. An equipment list is not a readiness inspection, and a training list is not practical authorization. External assessments can be accepted when their scope and evidence are equivalent; a platform name alone should neither approve nor disqualify the company.

### Deeper application

Sample evidence against mobilization rather than an ideal corporate roster. Trace a named person's credential to issuer verification, matching task scope and employer authorization; trace a named asset to the readiness evidence required for its use. A large file package can contain many irrelevant records. Accepting an equivalent external assessment requires checking what was actually examined, by whom and when. Requiring a duplicate upload in a preferred format does not resolve a substantive mismatch in people or equipment.

### Worked oilfield example

A subcontractor uploads operator cards, but the roster contains different workers from those assigned. The decision is to verify the assigned workers and matching task authorization before accepting the roster.

Evidence must correspond to the people actually performing the task; unrelated cards cannot transfer competence. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A checked roster connecting assigned people to authentic scoped credentials and employer authorization. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that two credentials expire before the planned mobilization date. The appropriate correction is to obtain valid matching evidence or assign appropriately authorized replacements before release. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 — Bridge shared responsibilities
lessons.body:
## Bridge shared responsibilities

A bridge identifies interfaces between employers and site operations: who issues permits, controls isolations, reports events, supervises workers and activates emergency response. Name responsible roles and communication routes. Do not simply write that both parties are responsible. Where responsibilities overlap, specify the handoff and acknowledgment. The subcontractor remains accountable for its workforce even when the host controls an operating system.

### Deeper application

A useful responsibility bridge follows a function to its handoff. For an emergency, identify who detects and raises the alarm, who supplies response capability, how responders gain access and who stops dependent operations. For permits, identify who requests, issues, holds and hands back the work. Write how each party knows the previous step is complete. Shared responsibility is not necessarily wrong, but an overlap needs an explicit coordination mechanism so each party does not assume the other acted.

### Worked oilfield example

The host assumes the subcontractor will arrange rescue; the subcontractor assumes the host provides it. The decision is to keep the dependent work unready until a suitable rescue interface is explicitly agreed and verified.

Shared assumptions can leave a critical function unprovided. A bridge must resolve who supplies and verifies it. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: An agreed interface record naming coverage, activation, access and responsibility acceptance. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the named rescue arrangement is unavailable on the intended night shift. The appropriate correction is to reconcile actual shift coverage and retain the dependent restriction until suitable coverage exists. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 4 — Resolve conflicting requirements
lessons.body:
## Resolve conflicting requirements

Compare the subcontractor's procedure with the Partner's site rules before work. A conflict may involve permit boundaries, reporting, supervision or a technical method. Do not let a worker choose whichever rule is easiest or assume the most restrictive-sounding wording solves incompatible systems. Appropriate authorities must resolve the conflict and issue a coherent work instruction. Preserve the original requirements and documented resolution.

### Deeper application

A conflict can involve incompatible sequencing rather than a simple stricter-or-looser rule. For example, one process may hand equipment back after mechanical checks while another requires an operating release still outstanding. Choosing whichever sounds more conservative may not identify the correct authority. Preserve both requirements, define the actual conflict and obtain a coordinated resolution. Communicate the resulting sequence to the people performing it; an agreement between managers does not reach the field automatically.

### Worked oilfield example

The subcontractor's handback process permits restart while the site's permit remains on hold. The decision is to resolve the conflicting restart requirements with the authorized employer and site roles before release.

Two incompatible release instructions create uncertainty that workers cannot safely resolve by guessing. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A documented conflict resolution identifying the applicable handback and site release sequence. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the resolution was agreed verbally but not passed to the incoming supervisor. The appropriate correction is to communicate the agreed sequence and confirm receipt before the next handback. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 5 — Flow requirements to further tiers
lessons.body:
## Flow requirements to further tiers

A subcontractor may engage another specialist, but that does not remove the original interface duties. Identify further tiers, actual scope and who verifies their prerequisites. Relevant requirements should reach the people performing the work in an understood form. Avoid unlimited copying of manuals without identifying which provisions apply. Changing the performing company or service triggers review of the bridge and acceptance evidence.

### Deeper application

Flowdown should be selective and explicit. Tell the lower tier which requirements apply to its actual scope, provide usable access and verify understanding. Sending an entire manual without explaining the relevant interfaces can leave the same gap hidden. The first subcontractor's promise to manage further tiers is not proof that qualification and site arrangements are implemented. Review who will verify them and what change requires notice, particularly when a new specialist, vehicle or hazardous service is introduced.

### Worked oilfield example

A cleaning subcontractor quietly hires a transport company that has not received the site's vehicle rules. The decision is to review the added tier and communicate applicable transport and site interfaces before its work begins.

The performing tier can introduce unassessed people and exposures; contractual distance does not eliminate the interface. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A lower-tier scope and acceptance record with relevant requirements and acknowledged site interfaces. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the further tier changes from domestic hauling to regulated cargo transport. The appropriate correction is to reassess the changed transport scope with the competent transport owner before dispatch. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 — Monitor performance and changes
lessons.body:
## Monitor performance and changes

Selection is an initial decision, not perpetual readiness. Monitor actual work, credential changes, unresolved findings and scope growth. Keep acceptance bounded and state restrictions. A serious field finding should reach the responsible operating authority even when the company score remains high. Reuse valid unchanged evidence, but do not stretch it to cover new work. Follow up corrective actions to see whether the control works in subsequent jobs.

### Deeper application

Monitoring should compare accepted scope with work observed. A subcontractor can perform routine jobs well while a newly added high-risk task remains unsupported. Review restrictions, expired evidence and recurring interface failures without restarting every unchanged assessment. If a finding affects current operations, route it promptly to the operating authority; do not wait for the next company score update. Conversely, an unsupported document claim should be corrected accurately without inventing an incident or assuming every task has failed.

### Worked oilfield example

A subcontractor repeatedly omits shift handovers despite a closed corrective action and favorable score. The decision is to escalate the verified failure, reopen the action and protect dependent work while the interface is corrected.

Monitoring tests real implementation; a grade or closed checkbox cannot refute an observed interface failure. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: Observed handovers and later field checks linked to the reopened corrective action. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that only office records were reviewed after the repeated field failure. The appropriate correction is to add suitable field observation and check later comparable handovers before claiming effectiveness. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A maintenance subcontractor adds vessel cleaning to its accepted work without presenting rescue or entry-role evidence. At the handover, a second issue is identified: Two credentials expire before the planned mobilization date. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Record both employers as responsible and begin. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Hold the added scope and obtain specialist evidence and interface review before mobilization. The reason is specific: Approval for one service does not establish competence or arrangements for a different exposure. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Obtain valid matching evidence or assign appropriately authorized replacements before release. The supporting record should show: A checked roster connecting assigned people to authentic scoped credentials and employer authorization. This is important because evidence must correspond to the people actually performing the task; unrelated cards cannot transfer competence. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because shared assumptions can leave a critical function unprovided. A bridge must resolve who supplies and verifies it. The suitable decision is: Keep the dependent work unready until a suitable rescue interface is explicitly agreed and verified. Evidence for review would include: An agreed interface record naming coverage, activation, access and responsibility acceptance. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

The subcontractor's handback process permits restart while the site's permit remains on hold. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The further tier changes from domestic hauling to regulated cargo transport. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Keep acceptance unrestricted because the score exceeds the threshold. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Resolve the conflicting restart requirements with the authorized employer and site roles before release. The reason is specific: Two incompatible release instructions create uncertainty that workers cannot safely resolve by guessing. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Reassess the changed transport scope with the competent transport owner before dispatch. The supporting record should show: A lower-tier scope and acceptance record with relevant requirements and acknowledged site interfaces. This is important because the performing tier can introduce unassessed people and exposures; contractual distance does not eliminate the interface. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because monitoring tests real implementation; a grade or closed checkbox cannot refute an observed interface failure. The suitable decision is: Escalate the verified failure, reopen the action and protect dependent work while the interface is corrected. Evidence for review would include: Observed handovers and later field checks linked to the reopened corrective action. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

Identify conflicting rules and responsibility boundaries; bridging case exercise. An appropriate assessor must have the knowledge and practical experience relevant to the role being judged. The employer must identify the applicable task standard, arrange safe supervised practice and evaluate performance against that standard. Use simulation for judgment and communication where appropriate; never create hazardous exposure to make a demonstration realistic. Record whether each item was observed, met the standard, needed practice or was not assessed. A gap needs feedback, additional practice and reassessment before authorization is expanded.

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.
